title: Fix malformed tool registration and lookup spec steps
description: Corrects two malformed algorithmic steps in the spec: reorders and separates the tool name validation and description emptiness checks in `registerTool`, and fixes a broken `If` statement (changed to `Let`) in the `getTools` lookup logic. These are editorial/correctness fixes to the specification prose, not behavioral changes.
impact: Implementors reading the spec get clearer, correctly structured algorithm steps with no change to the intended behavior.
author: emecii

title: Fix spelling of 'implementers' in documentation
description: Corrects the spelling of 'implementors' to 'implementers' in the Current Gaps section to match the consistent spelling used throughout the rest of the repository. This is a purely cosmetic documentation fix with no functional changes.
impact: No impact on developers or implementations; documentation text only.
author: lazizbekravshanov

title: Improve Readability and Wording in Life-of-a-Task Docs
description: Rewrites the life-of-a-task documentation for improved clarity and readability without changing any technical content. Sentences are shortened, passive constructions are replaced with active voice, and phrasing is made more direct throughout the document.
impact: Developers reading the A2A protocol documentation will find the life-of-a-task concepts easier to follow; no implementation changes are required.
author: msampathkumar

title: Improve readability and wording in key-concepts docs
description: Refactors the key-concepts.md documentation to improve clarity and conciseness. Sentences are shortened, passive constructions are replaced with active voice, and redundant phrasing is removed throughout the document.
impact: Documentation readers benefit from clearer explanations; no functional or protocol changes affect implementers.
author: msampathkumar

title: Improve Readability and Add Conceptual Section to A2A-MCP Docs
description: Rewrites the a2a-and-mcp documentation topic for improved clarity, conciseness, and plain-language wording throughout. Adds a new 'Horizontal and Vertical Layers' introductory section that frames MCP as vertical (deepening a single agent) and A2A as horizontal (connecting agents across boundaries). Existing sections are restructured with shorter sentences and clearer formatting for list items.
impact: Documentation readers and developers learning the A2A/MCP relationship will find the content easier to read and understand, with no changes to protocol behavior or API contracts.
author: msampathkumar

title: Improve Readability and Wording in What-is-A2A Docs
description: Rewrites the 'What is A2A?' documentation page for clarity and conciseness, simplifying sentence structure and replacing verbose phrasing throughout. Additional improvements include splitting the monolithic lifecycle Mermaid diagram into three staged diagrams, renaming the 'A2A and ADK' section to 'A2A and Agent Frameworks' to be framework-agnostic, and expanding the 'What's Next' section with multiple learning path options.
impact: Documentation readers benefit from clearer explanations; no API or protocol changes are introduced.
author: msampathkumar

title: Fix Off-Site Links Incorrectly Resolved as Internal in Link Checker
description: The docs link checker now correctly skips protocol-relative URLs, non-HTTP schemes (ftp, ws, vscode, mailto, tel), and other off-site link patterns instead of resolving them against the local build, which previously caused spurious 'Not Found' failures. A comprehensive unit test suite was added to enforce link classification rules, and the test runner is registered as a pre-commit hook.
impact: Documentation contributors and CI pipelines will no longer see false-positive broken link errors for valid external URLs with non-HTTP schemes or protocol-relative paths.
author: Ectsang

title: Add collision-safe KeyRing rename API with deprecation
description: Introduces `try_rename_key` returning `Result<(), OperationError>` that explicitly guards against missing source keys and occupied destination identifiers. The existing `rename_key` method is deprecated with a note directing users to the new API, and a new `OperationError` enum exposes the two failure modes.
impact: Developers using `KeyRing::rename_key` will see deprecation warnings and should migrate to `try_rename_key` to safely handle destination key conflicts.
author: erayack

title: Broaden executeTool() inputObject parameter type to any
description: Changes the `inputObject` parameter of `executeTool()` from `object` to `any` in the WebIDL interface, removing the default value `{}`. A runtime check is added to the algorithm that explicitly rejects with a `TypeError` if the provided value is not an Object, preserving the effective constraint while allowing broader input types at the IDL level.
impact: Developers implementing or consuming the ModelContext API should note that non-object inputs to `executeTool()` now produce an explicit `TypeError` rejection rather than being rejected at the WebIDL binding layer, and the parameter no longer defaults to `{}`.
author: beaufortfrancois

title: Upgrade js-yaml to 4.3.2 for CVE Fix
description: Bumps the js-yaml dependency from 4.3.1 to 4.3.2 to address CVE-2026-84375, a security vulnerability. The change updates both package.json overrides and the lockfile integrity hash.
impact: Developers using this repository's tooling will receive a security fix with no API or behavioral changes.
author: damaz91

title: Add Loyalty Extension Specification to 2026-04-08 Release
description: Backports the loyalty extension specification to the 2026-04-08 release, introducing a new `loyalty.json` schema and comprehensive `loyalty.md` documentation covering memberships, tiers, benefits, and rewards. The extension enables loyalty program integration across catalog search, catalog lookup, cart, and checkout capabilities with support for provisional membership claims and monetary benefit attribution.
impact: Developers implementing catalog, cart, or checkout capabilities can now optionally support the loyalty extension to surface member-specific pricing, tier status, and reward earning forecasts during agentic shopping flows.
author: damaz91

title: Add Origin Field to Observed Tool Collection Struct
description: Introduces a new `observed tool collection` struct that wraps tool definitions with an explicit `origin` field in the observation tool map. This replaces the previous approach of a plain list of tool definitions as map values, and formalizes origin exposure as a structured requirement rather than an implementation advisement.
impact: Implementers of the observation tool map must update their data structures to use the new `observed tool collection` struct (containing `origin` and `tools` fields) instead of a bare list of tool definitions.
author: johannhof

title: Bump mkdocs-material dependency from 9.7.6 to 9.7.7
description: Updates the mkdocs-material documentation theme from version 9.7.6 to 9.7.7 in the lock file. This is a routine patch-level dependency update with no changes to the protocol specification itself.
impact: No impact on protocol implementers; only affects contributors building the documentation site locally.
author: dependabot[bot]

title: Announce Payments Technical Council Inaugural Members
description: Adds an announcement entry to the documentation page introducing the formation of the Payments Technical Council (Payments TC) and its eight inaugural members. The announcement references the closed nomination process and links to the corresponding GitHub Discussion #798 for full details.
impact: Documentation readers and protocol participants are informed of the new governance body; no API or specification changes are introduced.
author: damaz91

title: Expand lockfile registry blocking to npm and more sources
description: Extends the pre-commit hook to block non-public registries in both `uv.lock` and `package-lock.json`. The Python registry check is broadened to catch CodeArtifact, AWS, Azure DevOps, and any non-pypi.org registry URLs, while a new npm hook blocks any resolved packages not coming from registry.npmjs.org.
impact: Contributors whose local environments resolve packages from private or corporate registries will have commits blocked and must run `uv lock --refresh` or `npm install` pointed at the public registry to proceed.
author: ptiper

title: Bump fast-uri dependency to fix security vulnerability
description: Updates the fast-uri package override from ^3.1.2 to ^3.1.6 (resolving to 3.1.7) to address a known vulnerability. This is a dev dependency override change with no impact on the protocol specification itself.
impact: Repository maintainers and contributors benefit from a more secure development toolchain; no changes to the protocol specification or consumer-facing APIs.
author: carolinerg1

title: Remove stale example corpus counts from docs
description: Updates the documentation comment in the validation script to remove hardcoded counts (268 JSON blocks, 39 spec docs) that had become stale. The reference is replaced with generic language that won't require updates as the corpus grows.
impact: No functional impact; affects only developers reading the validation script's documentation comments.
author: FanouZeng-TT

title: Enforce Whole-Word Skip and Non-Empty Reason in Annotations
description: Updates `parse_annotation` to use a whole-word regex match for `skip` (preventing typos like `skiped` or `skip_the_check` from silently disabling validation) and requires a non-empty `reason="..."` field, returning an error if missing. This ensures every skipped example remains auditable.
impact: Maintainers writing example annotations must now include a non-empty `reason="..."` alongside `skip`; bare `skip` or `skip reason=""` will be rejected by the validator.
author: Ectsang

title: Improve Key Resolution and Directory Validation in Verifier
description: Updates the verifier to resolve keys by cryptographic thumbprint instead of the `kid` claim, allowing correct matching even when `kid` values differ. Also adds a maximum key limit (100) for directories and applies full `directoryFromUnknown` validation when parsing inline JWKS from signature agent cards.
impact: Developers using the verification worker example will benefit from more robust key resolution and stricter directory validation, with no changes required to existing integrations.
author: thibmeu

title: Add JWK Security Guidance and Test Key Warnings
description: Adds explicit warnings that RFC 9421 test keys must not be used in production, with links to security considerations. Expands the Security Considerations section with actionable guidance on generating unique asymmetric keys, publishing only public JWK values, and overlapping keys during rotation.
impact: Developers implementing web-bot-auth should review the updated Security Considerations section to ensure they are using production-appropriate keys instead of the published RFC test keys.
author: thibmeu

title: Fix inaccurate descriptions in documentation files
description: Corrects three documentation inaccuracies: updates the Cloudflare Workers example description to accurately reflect its signing and verification behavior, clarifies Caddy plugin key-loading behavior and `fail_on_load_error` semantics, and adds guidance on using the `label` parameter for multi-signature verification in the web-bot-auth package.
impact: Developers reading the documentation will get more accurate descriptions of example behavior and configuration options, with no changes to any code or protocol.
author: thibmeu

title: Reclassify Headless Browsing as Supported Use Case
description: Moves headless browsing scenarios from Non-Goals to Goals, acknowledging that tools designed for human-in-the-loop workflows can also serve headless task completion. The Non-Goals section is updated to clarify that fully autonomous, purely server-side workflows remain out of scope.
impact: Developers building headless or hybrid human/headless browser integrations will find clearer guidance that WebMCP supports their use cases, while purely server-side automation remains explicitly out of scope.
author: sdras

title: Document Chrome flag for local WebMCP development
description: Adds a reference to the `about:flags#enable-webmcp-testing` Chrome flag in the implementation status documentation, linking to the official Chrome developer guide for local WebMCP development. This helps developers test WebMCP locally without needing Origin Trial access.
impact: Developers looking to test WebMCP locally in Chrome can now find the required flag directly in the implementation status documentation.
author: beaufortfrancois

title: Update Documentation Examples to Current modelContext API
description: Replaces stale references to the old `agent` object and `provideContext` method with the current `modelContext` API across README, declarative API explainer, and service workers documentation. Also corrects an outdated anchor link for `ToolExecuteCallbackOptions.signal` and renames the `agent` callback parameter to `options` in tool execute signatures.
impact: Developers referencing the explainer documentation will now see accurate, up-to-date API examples that match the current WebMCP specification.
author: lazizbekravshanov

title: Fix JSON-LD Media Type in Declarative API Explainer
description: Corrects an incorrect JSON-LD media type from `application/json-ld` to the standardized `application/ld+json` in the declarative API explainer documentation. This ensures the spec references the correct MIME type as defined by the JSON-LD specification.
impact: Developers reading the explainer will now see the correct `application/ld+json` media type, preventing potential misimplementation of script tag extraction logic.
author: lazizbekravshanov

title: Add Best Practices Section for Tool Design Guidance
description: Adds a comprehensive Best Practices section to the README covering tool strategy, naming conventions, schema design, and error handling for WebMCP tool authors. Also adds inline guidance on dynamic tool registration patterns to manage agent context window limitations.
impact: Developers implementing WebMCP tools gain actionable guidance on tool budget management, dynamic registration patterns, and schema design to improve agent performance.
author: beaufortfrancois

title: Replace flowcharts with sequence diagrams in README
description: Converts both the WebMCP in-browser tool flow and direct backend MCP flow diagrams from Mermaid `graph TD` flowcharts to `sequenceDiagram` format. The new diagrams add step-by-step message flow detail, including API responses, tool results, and clarifying notes about state synchronization challenges.
impact: Documentation readers and contributors benefit from clearer, more detailed protocol flow diagrams; no implementation changes required.
author: domfarolino

title: Add consequentialHint Boolean Field to ToolAnnotations
description: Adds a new `consequentialHint` boolean field to the `ToolAnnotations` dictionary, initially defaulting to false. When set to true, this field signals that a tool performs significant, real-world, or non-reversible actions (e.g., booking flights, transferring money), enabling clients and agents to enforce mandatory user confirmation before execution. The change also includes a corresponding security mitigation section documenting the annotation's role in addressing misrepresentation-of-intent threats.
impact: Developers implementing tool registration and `getTools` flows should update their `ToolAnnotations` handling to expose the new `consequentialHint` field; clients and agents can optionally use this hint to gate high-stakes tool executions behind user confirmation prompts.
author: beaufortfrancois

title: Add Agent Support to Implementation Status Documentation
description: Updates the implementation status documentation to include AI agents (e.g., ChatGPT Desktop) alongside browsers. The document title, description, and README reference are updated to reflect that WebMCP support is tracked for both browsers and agents.
impact: Developers and integrators checking WebMCP compatibility can now reference implementation status for AI agents in addition to browsers.
author: beaufortfrancois

title: Add Blog Post Excerpts with 'Continue Reading' Links
description: Adds `<!-- more -->` excerpt markers to blog posts so the index page displays truncated previews instead of full content. Also updates the announcement banner to highlight the AAIF membership post and increases blog pagination from 1 to 2 posts per page.
impact: Documentation site visitors will see blog post excerpts with 'Continue reading' links on the blog index, improving navigation and content discoverability.
author: msampathkumar

title: Add FAF to official partners list
description: Adds FAF (https://faf.one/) to the partners list in the documentation. This is a purely additive documentation change with no impact on the protocol specification itself.
impact: No impact on developers or implementers; documentation-only change adding a new partner entry.
author: Wolfe-Jam

title: Clarify Hybrid Agents documentation in Life of a Task
description: Rewrites the Hybrid Agents section in the 'Life of a Task' doc to improve clarity around when Message versus Task objects are used. Adds a plain-language explanation that Messages handle lightweight negotiation while Tasks represent committed, observable work, and removes a redundant concluding sentence.
impact: Developers reading the protocol documentation will have a clearer understanding of Hybrid Agent behavior; no implementation changes required.
author: madankumarpichamuthu

title: Fix broken Starlette documentation link
description: Updates the Starlette framework URL in the Python tutorial from `starlette.io` to `starlette.dev`. The previous link was broken and pointed to an incorrect domain.
impact: Developers following the Python A2A server tutorial will now reach the correct Starlette documentation site.
author: keraron

title: Pre-compute Ed25519 Verifying Keys at Import Time
description: Refactors the `KeyRing` internals to prepare `ed25519_dalek::VerifyingKey` instances once during key import rather than reconstructing them on every verification call. A new `KeyEntry` struct stores both the raw key material (preserving the existing public `get` API) and a `PreparedKey` enum used internally by `get_prepared` during signature verification. A benchmark crate is also added to measure the performance impact of this optimization.
impact: Developers using the `web-bot-auth` crate benefit from reduced per-request cryptographic overhead; no changes to the public API are required.
author: benni-rogge

title: Switch to Package-Specific npm Publish Tags
description: Updates the GitHub Actions publish workflow to use package-specific git tags (e.g., `http-message-sig@x.y.z`) instead of a generic `v*` pattern, enabling independent releases per package. Each publish step now also validates that the git tag version matches the corresponding `package.json` version before publishing.
impact: Repository maintainers must use package-specific tags (e.g., `http-message-sig@1.0.0`) instead of generic `v*` tags when triggering npm releases.
author: thibmeu

title: Bump dev dependency packages across examples
description: Updates four dev dependencies: `@types/chrome` from 0.2.6 to 0.2.7, `@cloudflare/workers-types` from 5.20260819.1 to 5.20260826.1, `wrangler` from 4.110.0 to 4.126.0, and `oxlint` from 1.79.0 to 1.80.0. The package-lock.json is also updated to reflect the resolved transitive dependencies for the new wrangler version.
impact: Developers working on the browser-extension and verification-workers examples will pull updated dev tooling on next install; no runtime or protocol behavior is affected.
author: dependabot[bot]

title: Bump log dependency from 0.4.33 to 0.4.34
description: Updates the `log` crate from version 0.4.33 to 0.4.34 in the Rust dependency lockfile. This is a routine patch-level dependency update with no API changes.
impact: No impact on developers or implementers; this is an internal dependency update with no functional changes.
author: dependabot[bot]

title: Rewrite http-message-sig with explicit RFC 9421 API
description: The `http-message-sig` package has been rewritten with an explicit RFC 9421-compliant API, bumping it from v0.2.0 to v0.3.0 and `web-bot-auth` from v0.1.3 to v0.2.0. The new API replaces implicit helpers like `signatureHeadersSync`, `recommendedComponents`, and `directoryResponseHeaders` with explicit primitives (`sign`, `signSync`, `verify`, `createSignature`) and a resolver-based verification model. Examples and internal implementations have been updated to use the new structured interfaces including `WebBotSigner`, `WebBotSignerSync`, `RequestDescriptor`, and `ResponseDescriptor`.
impact: Developers using `http-message-sig` or `web-bot-auth` must migrate to the new RFC 9421 API, replacing removed exports (`signatureHeaders`, `recommendedComponents`, `directoryResponseHeaders`, `helpers`, `Signer`, `VerificationParams`, etc.) with the new `sign`/`verify`/`createSignature` functions and updated signer/verifier interfaces.
author: thibmeu

title: Rename PushNotificationConfig to TaskPushNotificationConfig in Docs
description: Renames all references to `PushNotificationConfig` to `TaskPushNotificationConfig` across the protocol specification and streaming/async topic documentation. This aligns the object name with its task-scoped context and matches the naming convention already used in related RPC methods like `CreateTaskPushNotificationConfig`.
impact: Developers referencing the specification docs must use the updated type name `TaskPushNotificationConfig`; implementations targeting the actual proto/API schema are unaffected by this documentation-only rename.
author: Iwaniukooo11

title: Fix Incorrect Pagination and Protocol Field Names in Docs
description: Corrects field name references in migration documentation: replaces `protocolVersions` with `protocolVersion` in `supportedInterfaces` entries, and fixes pagination variable names from `cursor`/`nextCursor`/`limit` to `pageToken`/`nextPageToken`/`pageSize`. These are documentation-only fixes ensuring the migration guide matches the actual v1.0 protocol specification.
impact: Developers following the migration guide to upgrade to v1.0 will now see accurate field names, preventing implementation errors when handling pagination and protocol version detection.
author: sachinsharma3191

title: Add Blog Section with A2A Joins AAIF Announcement
description: Introduces a structured blog section to the documentation site using MkDocs blog plugin, migrating the existing v1.0 announcement post and adding a new post about A2A joining the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) as a Growth Stage project. A redirect is added for the old announcement URL to maintain link compatibility.
impact: Documentation site visitors gain a blog index with structured posts; existing links to `announcing-1.0.md` are redirected automatically, so no action is required from developers or users.
author: msampathkumar

title: Add New Capabilities and Extensions for v2026-08-25
description: Updates core concepts documentation to reflect new capabilities and extensions introduced in the v2026-08-25 protocol version. Adds three new capabilities (permalink, location search, location lookup) and three new extensions (loyalty, split payments, payment terms), and clarifies that services apply to both vertical and common domains.
impact: Developers implementing UCP integrations should review the new capabilities and extensions to determine if they need to support permalink sharing, location lookup, loyalty programs, split payments, or payment terms in their implementations.
author: ptiper

title: Add v2026-08-25 Protocol Release Announcement to Docs
description: Adds the v2026-08-25 protocol release announcement to the announcements page, highlighting major enhancements including multi-vertical expansion, 3DS2 payments security, structured request constraints, independent capability versioning, and grocery shopping readiness. Also registers the new release's llms.txt index in mkdocs.yml for LLM-accessible spec discovery.
impact: Developers and integrators following UCP announcements will see the new v2026-08-25 release noted on ucp.dev, with a link to the full release notes for protocol changes.
author: carolinerg1

title: Add Signed Directory Response Test Vectors
description: Adds `content-digest` to the required response signature components and introduces a new test vector set for signed directory responses. A new JSON test vector file, generator script, and verification test are added to validate that directory responses correctly bind the response body to the request authority via HTTP message signatures.
impact: Implementors verifying directory responses must now include `content-digest` in the signed components; existing signatures that omit it will fail verification against the updated spec.
author: thibmeu

title: Bump development dependency packages across examples
description: Updates six development dependencies: `@types/chrome` (0.2.5→0.2.6), `@cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers` (0.21.2→0.22.0), `@cloudflare/workers-types` (5.20260729.1→5.20260819.1), `oxlint` (1.78.0→1.79.0), `vitest` (4.1.10→4.1.11), and associated transitive dependencies including workerd binaries. Also removes unused optional packages `@emnapi/core`, `@emnapi/wasi-threads`, and `@napi-rs/wasm-runtime` from the lockfile.
impact: Developers working on the browser extension or verification workers examples will get updated tooling versions; no changes to the protocol specification or runtime behavior.
author: dependabot[bot]

title: Clarify exposedTo option description in README
description: Fixes a grammatical issue and improves clarity in the sentence describing the `exposedTo` option for cross-origin iframe tool exposure. The phrase 'of their choice, `exposedTo` option during registration' was corrected to 'via the `exposedTo` option', making the sentence more precise and readable.
impact: Documentation readers and implementers benefit from clearer wording around the `exposedTo` registration option, with no behavioral or API changes required.
author: marcianoskate

title: Add ChatGPT Desktop to WebMCP implementation status
description: Adds ChatGPT Desktop as a supported WebMCP implementation in the implementation-status.md document, along with OpenAI SVG logo assets (light and dark variants). The entry includes a navigation icon with dark/light mode support and a link to the ChatGPT Desktop download page.
impact: Developers and users referencing the implementation status document will now see ChatGPT Desktop listed as a supported WebMCP client.
author: nmccormack-oai

title: Update Documentation Links to Remove Stale Issue References
description: Removes closed GitHub issue links from explainer documents and replaces stale PR links with direct links to the merged declarative API explainer file. Also clarifies the description of in-page agent tool discovery using `getTools()` and `executeTool()` APIs.
impact: Readers and implementers following documentation links will now be directed to stable file URLs instead of closed issues or merged PRs.
author: HaoChiBao

title: Add Tieqi Tech and TiEQi-A2A as A2A Partners
description: Adds Tieqi Tech (铁旗科技) to the partners list in the documentation and registers TiEQi-A2A as a known A2A agent deployment. This is a documentation-only change to the partners registry.
impact: No impact on developers or implementers; this is a purely informational documentation update adding a new partner entry.
author: iTiEQi

title: Add Discord Server Links Across Documentation
description: Adds the official A2A Discord server link (https://discord.gg/a2aprotocol) across multiple documentation files including README, CONTRIBUTING, GOVERNANCE, community docs, and tutorials. Also fixes an HTTP link to HTTPS in GOVERNANCE.md and adds Discord as a resource in the PR template for maintainer onboarding.
impact: Community members and contributors will now find Discord links prominently in all key entry points, making it easier to discover and join the A2A community chat.
author: keraron

title: Add OpenAgents to Partners List
description: Adds OpenAgents (openagents.org) to the official partners list in the documentation. This is a purely additive documentation change with no impact on the protocol specification itself.
impact: No technical impact on developers; serves as a reference update for users browsing the partners directory.
author: zomux

title: Add Rust SDK and Main Repo Maintainers
description: Adds maintainer entries for the core `a2a` repository and the new `a2a-rs` (Rust) SDK repository to MAINTAINERS.md. Four maintainers are assigned to each repository with the `maintain` role.
impact: Project contributors and community members can now identify the designated maintainers for the main a2a repository and the Rust SDK repository.
author: muscariello

title: Add Location Search and Lookup Capabilities to Specification
description: Introduces two new common capabilities: `dev.ucp.common.location.search` for querying physical locations via free-text, spatial relations (distance/serves), and filters (hours, amenities, items), and `dev.ucp.common.location.lookup` for retrieving full location details by identifier. The specification includes detailed operating hours semantics, amenity vocabulary, item availability filtering, and REST/MCP transport bindings, plus integration guidance with Shopping capabilities like Catalog, Cart, and Checkout.
impact: Developers implementing platform integrations must add support for the new location search and lookup endpoints, and those implementing catalog, cart, and checkout flows must handle the new location-related fields and destination selection patterns introduced across the shopping specification.
author: jingyli
reasons: breaking, on planned surface: ap2-mandate-instrument, commerce-observation

title: Move Payment Constructs from Shopping to Common Namespace
description: Refactors payment-related constructs, schemas, and extensions from the `shopping/` path and `dev.ucp.shopping.*` namespace to `common/` path and `dev.ucp.common.payment.*` namespace. This includes payment authentication, AP2 mandates, split payments, and all related JSON schema references. All internal documentation links and schema paths have been updated accordingly.
impact: Developers and integrators referencing payment extension identifiers (e.g., `dev.ucp.shopping.ap2_mandate`, `dev.ucp.shopping.split_payments`) or schema paths (e.g., `schemas/shopping/types/payment_credential.json`) must update to the new `dev.ucp.common.payment.*` identifiers and `schemas/common/types/` paths.
author: jingyli

title: Fix Invalid JSONPath for Discount Allocation Targets
description: Corrects the JSONPath expression for targeting totals in discount allocations, replacing the invalid `$.totals.shipping` path with a valid RFC 9535 filter expression `$.totals[?@.type == "fulfillment"]`. Both the documentation examples and the JSON schema description string are updated to reflect the correct path syntax.
impact: Developers implementing discount allocation targeting against totals should update their JSONPath expressions to use the RFC 9535 filter syntax shown in the corrected examples.
author: sakinaroufid

title: Reorganize Shopping Extensions Into Nested Subfolder Structure
description: Moves shopping extension spec files (buyer-consent, discount, fulfillment) from the root specification directory into `docs/specification/shopping/extensions/` and loyalty into `docs/specification/common/extensions/`. All internal cross-references, example spec URLs, and redirect rules in mkdocs.yml and hooks.py are updated to reflect the new paths.
impact: Documentation readers and tooling that hardcodes old spec URLs (e.g., `/specification/fulfillment`, `/specification/discount`) will be redirected via updated redirect rules, but implementers referencing spec URLs in profiles should update to the new canonical paths such as `/specification/shopping/extensions/fulfillment`.
author: niranjanmanjunath

title: Replace inventory filtering with item availability filter
description: Renames and redefines the `filters.inventory` predicate to `filters.items` across Location Search and Lookup capabilities, clarifying it as a coarse, provisional item availability check rather than inventory detail. Updates schemas, OpenAPI/OpenRPC specs, and all documentation to reflect the new terminology and semantics, including explicit guidance that unknown or unevaluable item identifiers result in silent omission rather than errors.
impact: Developers implementing Location Search or Lookup with inventory filtering must rename `filters.inventory` to `filters.items` in their requests and update response handling logic accordingly.
author: igrigorik

title: Refactor Token Binding to Be Vertical-Agnostic
description: Replaces the checkout-specific `checkout_id` field in the binding object with a generic `type` and `id` structure, and separates the `identity` field from the `binding` object into a top-level field. This makes token binding applicable across different protocol verticals beyond just shopping/checkout flows.
impact: Implementors of payment handler tokenization flows must update their detokenize request payloads to use `binding.type` and `binding.id` instead of `binding.checkout_id`, and move `identity` out of the `binding` object to the request top level.
author: prasad-stripe
reasons: breaking, on planned surface: ap2-mandate-instrument, commerce-observation

title: Change Location Amenities from Array to Descriptor Map
description: Replaces the flat reverse-DNS array representation of location amenities with a map keyed by amenity identifier, where each entry contains a mandatory buyer-facing `description` string. This makes amenities self-describing, enabling platforms to render custom or unrecognized amenities without requiring a shared vocabulary lookup. Schema changes affect `location.json`, `location_filter.json`, and `location_destination.json`.
impact: Businesses implementing the Location capability must update their amenity responses from a string array to an object map with `description` fields per entry; Platforms must update parsing logic and validate that all amenity entries include a non-empty description.
author: igrigorik

title: Clarify resource binding vs participant authorization in tokenization
description: Separates the concepts of resource binding (`binding` object with `type`/`id`) from participant authorization (`identity`) in the tokenization specification. Adds explicit rule that every token is issued to exactly one participant, with mandatory verification of both participant identity and caller authority on detokenize. Clarifies that unknown `binding` members must be ignored rather than rejected during equality comparison.
impact: Tokenizer implementers must ensure their detokenization logic explicitly records the issued-to participant at tokenize time and verifies both participant match and caller authority at detokenize time, and must ignore unrecognized binding fields rather than rejecting them.
author: igrigorik

title: Remove Deprecated ID Field and Clean Up Schema
description: Removes the deprecated `id` field from cart update request schemas, examples, and scaffolds, replacing transition-based `ucp_request` definitions with unified single-value annotations. Also fixes a fulfillment method field that was incorrectly marked as `optional` on create instead of `omit`.
impact: Implementers sending `id` in cart update request bodies must remove it, as it is no longer part of the schema; identification must be done exclusively via URL path parameter.
author: jingyli

title: Split PAN and Network Token credential types, use Constraint Expressions for instrument requirements
description: This PR splits the monolithic `card_credential` type into separate `pan_credential` and `network_token_credential` schemas, each with its own `type` discriminator. It also replaces the shorthand `brands: [...]` constraint format in `available_instruments` with full Constraint Expressions (`properties.brand.enum`), aligning instrument requirements with the existing request constraints grammar.
impact: Implementers of payment handlers, business profiles, and checkout flows must update `available_instruments` constraints from `{"brands": [...]}` to `{"properties": {"brand": {"enum": [...]}}}`, and update credential handling to use the new `pan_credential` and `network_token_credential` schemas instead of the unified `card_credential` type.
author: raginpirate

title: Fix Fragment Preservation in Root Spec Links
description: Fixes a bug in `hooks.py` where URL fragments (anchors) were stripped when rewriting specification links to the `latest/` path. Also improves `check_links.py` to explicitly reject links targeting raw `.md` files before applying ignore patterns, ensuring rendered HTML pages are always linked instead of source markdown.
impact: Developers and documentation maintainers benefit from correct anchor navigation in generated spec links, and the link checker now catches raw Markdown links even when they match ignore patterns.
author: igrigorik

title: Remove Orphaned account_info JSON Schema File
description: Deletes the unused `account_info.json` schema file from the shopping types directory. This schema defined a `Payment Account Info` object with an EMVCo PAR field but was no longer referenced by any other part of the specification.
impact: Developers who may have been referencing this schema file directly by its `$id` URI should note its removal, though its orphaned status suggests no active consumers.
author: raginpirate
reasons: payment on defect-vocabulary, ap2-mandate-instrument, commerce-observation, discovery

title: Add anyOf constraint to request_constraints schema
description: Introduces an `anyOf` keyword to Object Constraints in `constraint_expression.json` and `request_constraints.json`, enabling conditional/alternative validation branches. Also adds `minItems`/`minProperties` guards to existing `required` and `properties` fields, and documents the feature with a payments credential discrimination example. A fix for self-referential `#` JSON Schema refs in the docs renderer is included.
impact: Developers authoring request constraint schemas can now express mutually exclusive field requirements (e.g., different credential shapes) using `anyOf`; existing constraints are unaffected, but the new `minItems`/`minProperties` constraints may invalidate previously accepted empty `required` arrays or empty `properties` objects.
author: raginpirate

title: Clarify anyOf branch rules and improve constraint examples
description: Enforces that `anyOf` branches in constraint expressions must be non-empty by adding `minProperties: 1` validation to the JSON schemas, preventing empty branches that would neutralize alternation. Updates documentation to clarify that branches are alternatives (not partitions), adds guidance on using discriminator fields in `required` to make branches exclusive, and improves the credential constraint example to use typed discriminators.
impact: Schema authors using `anyOf` in request constraints must ensure all branches are non-empty; empty branches that were previously valid are now rejected by schema validation.
author: igrigorik

title: Skip Root Documentation Links in Spec-Only Build Verification
description: Adds a conditional link-ignore pattern in `check_links.py` that activates when `DOCS_MODE=spec`, suppressing false-positive broken link errors for `/documentation/` paths that only exist on the root site. This prevents spec-isolated builds from failing link checks due to cross-site references that are intentionally out of scope.
impact: CI pipelines running link checks against spec-only builds (with `DOCS_MODE=spec`) will no longer produce spurious failures for root documentation links.
author: damaz91

title: Refactor Location Spatial Relations and Lookup Correlation
description: Replaces the implicit geofence model with two explicit spatial relations: `distance` (proximity radius check) and `serves` (serviceability check), and overhauls the Lookup response to include an `inputs` correlation array per Location instead of relying on ID matching. The `location_filter`, `location_serves`, and related schemas are updated to reflect these distinct, named relations, and pagination defaults are clarified with RECOMMENDED wording rather than a hard default.
impact: Developers implementing Location Search must update spatial filter logic to use the new explicit `distance`/`serves` relations, and those implementing Lookup must populate the `inputs` array on each returned Location to enable proper Platform-side correlation.
author: igrigorik

title: Remove deprecated id field from checkout update examples
description: Removes the deprecated `id` field from three checkout update request body examples in the REST specification docs. The `id` was previously marked as deprecated since it is redundant with the checkout ID already provided in the URL path.
impact: Developers referencing these docs will see cleaner examples without the deprecated field, but no functional changes are required to existing implementations.
author: raginpirate

title: Move Primitive Types from Shopping to Common Namespace
description: Relocates six schema types (context, policy, price_filter, price_range, signals, total/totals) from `source/schemas/shopping/types/` to `source/schemas/common/types/`, updating their `$id` URIs and internal `$ref` paths accordingly. All dependent shopping schemas (cart, catalog_lookup, catalog_search, checkout, order, and shopping subtypes) are updated to reference the new common paths.
impact: Implementors and integrators referencing schema `$id` URIs or `$ref` paths under `shopping/types/` for context, policy, price_filter, price_range, signals, total, or totals must update their references to the new `common/types/` paths.
author: jingyli

title: Reorganize specification docs into domain vertical hierarchy
description: Restructures the specification directory by grouping documents under domain verticals (Shopping, Payment, Common), moving files like checkout, order, identity-linking, and payment guides into their respective subdirectories. Updates all internal cross-references, navigation links, and URL paths to reflect the new hierarchy, and replaces hardcoded version strings with `{{ ucp_version }}` template variables.
impact: Documentation site maintainers and contributors must use updated file paths and URLs; external links to specification pages (e.g., `/specification/checkout/`) will break and need to be updated to the new domain-prefixed paths (e.g., `/specification/shopping/checkout/`).
author: niranjanmanjunath

title: Add Response-Carried Request Constraints Protocol Member
description: Introduces `ucp.request_constraints`, a new response-only protocol member that allows a Business to declare machine-evaluable constraints on the next Platform request (e.g., required fields, enum/const value restrictions). The feature includes a JSONPath-based targeting mechanism, a closed Constraint Expression grammar backed by new JSON Schema files, and defined lifecycle/scoping rules for constraint sets across request/response cycles.
impact: Platform implementers gain an optional preflight evaluation capability to validate request data against Business-declared constraints before submission, reducing round trips; Business implementers must conform to the new `request_constraints` schema when emitting constraints in authoritative responses.
author: igrigorik

title: Add Path Targeting to Request Constraints
description: Adds an optional `path` field to the `request_constraints` schema, allowing a Business to specify an RFC 9535 JSONPath query that selects which objects in the next request a Constraint Expression applies to. When `path` is omitted, the effective path defaults to the Normalized Path from the authoritative response root to the structured object containing `request_constraints`. The validation model is updated from an `allOf` JSON Schema composition to an explicit path-selection-then-validate loop.
impact: Developers implementing Business-side constraint emission or Platform-side preflight logic must update to handle the new optional `path` field, support multi-object selection semantics, and apply overlapping-path rules when evaluating constraints.
author: igrigorik

title: Add Inline Comment Version Support to Super Linter Script
description: Updates `super_linter_local.py` to handle pinned-hash GitHub Action references with inline version comments (e.g., `@<sha> # v8.7.0`). The regex and version extraction logic are updated to prefer the comment-specified version over the hash, and raw text parsing is added to reliably extract the `uses:` line from the workflow file.
impact: Developers using `super_linter_local.py` with SHA-pinned super-linter action references and inline version comments will now correctly resolve the Docker image tag instead of failing or using the raw hash.
author: drewolson-google

title: Upgrade Super Linter to v8.7.0 with config updates
description: Upgrades the super-linter GitHub Action from v8.6.0 to v8.7.0, pinning action references to specific commit SHAs for improved security. Updates biome.json to use the new `preset` key instead of `recommended` and excludes SVG files in docs/assets from linting.
impact: No impact on protocol consumers; affects only CI/CD pipeline maintainers and contributors submitting PRs to this repository.
author: drewolson-google

title: Preserve In-Flight Tool Executions After Unregistration
description: Removes the logic that canceled pending tool executions upon tool unregistration, allowing in-flight executions to complete naturally. The unregistration process now only notifies documents of the tool change without interrupting active executions, and a related note/example about the unregistration race condition has been removed as it no longer applies.
impact: Developers implementing tool consumers should expect that unregistering a tool no longer aborts in-flight executions, meaning active `executeTool()` promises will now resolve or reject based on the tool's own completion rather than being forcibly canceled.
author: domfarolino

title: Add AbortSignal Integration for Tool Execution Cancellation
description: Implements AbortSignal integration for tool execution by introducing a local pending tool executions map on ModelContext and a new 'cancel a pending tool execution' algorithm. Tool execute callbacks now receive a uuid and an AbortController signal, enabling proper cancellation propagation from the caller's signal through to the tool's execution context, including handling race conditions between cancellation and natural resolution.
impact: Developers implementing tool execution handlers will now receive an AbortSignal via ToolExecuteCallbackOptions, allowing them to respond to cancellation requests from callers using executeTool() with an AbortSignal.
author: domfarolino

title: Update Todd Segal's Title to Distinguished Engineer
description: Updates Todd Segal's title in the governance committee table from 'Principal Engineer' to 'Distinguished Engineer'. This is a metadata/administrative change to keep the governance documentation accurate.
impact: No functional impact; governance document consumers will see the updated title for Google's TSC representative.
author: muscariello

title: Update ServiceNow TSC Representative in Governance Docs
description: Replaces Sean Hughes with Sugandh Rakha as the ServiceNow representative on the Technical Steering Committee in GOVERNANCE.md. The spelling allowlist is updated to accommodate the new representative's name and GitHub handle.
impact: Community members and contributors should note the updated ServiceNow point of contact for governance matters.
author: muscariello

title: Fix Schema Cache Isolation by Root Directory
description: The schema resolution cache key now includes the resolved `schema_base` path in addition to schema path, direction, and operation. Previously, schemas with identical paths but different root directories would incorrectly return cached results from the first root, causing validation to use wrong schema definitions.
impact: Developers running example validation scripts against multiple schema roots will now get correct, isolated schema resolution results instead of stale cross-root cache hits.
author: FanouZeng-TT

title: Add early validation for missing build dependencies
description: The build_local.sh script now checks for the presence of `cargo` and `ucp-schema` executables before proceeding, exiting with a descriptive error message if either is missing. This prevents cryptic downstream build failures by surfacing dependency issues immediately with actionable installation instructions.
impact: Developers running the local build script will receive clear, actionable error messages if Rust or ucp-schema are not installed, instead of failing with an obscure error later in the build process.
author: FanouZeng-TT

title: Add Explicit Type Discriminator to Fulfillment Destinations
description: Adds a required `type` field to fulfillment destination objects in Business responses, with well-known values `shipping_address` and `business_location`. The change formalizes destination typing rules: `type` is required in all Business responses but optional in Platform requests, and introduces a new `location_destination` schema replacing `retail_location` for Business Location Destinations.
impact: Businesses implementing fulfillment responses must now include an explicit `type` field on every destination object, and Platform implementers must update parsers to handle the typed destination discriminator.
author: igrigorik
reasons: breaking, on shipped surface: defect-vocabulary, discovery

title: Bump clap dependency from 4.6.5 to 4.6.6
description: Updates the clap CLI parsing library and its clap_builder sub-crate from version 4.6.5 to 4.6.6 in Cargo.lock. This is a routine patch-level dependency update with no changes to the protocol specification or public API.
impact: No impact on developers or implementers; this is an internal dependency lock file update only.
author: dependabot[bot]

title: Bump dev dependency packages to latest versions
description: Updates four development dependency packages: `@cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers` from 0.20.2 to 0.21.2, `oxlint` from 1.77.0 to 1.78.0, `@cloudflare/workers-types` to 5.20260815.1, and associated transitive dependencies including `miniflare` and `wrangler`. These are all dev dependencies used for testing and linting in the verification-workers example.
impact: Developers working on the repository locally will receive updated dev tooling; no changes to the protocol specification or runtime behavior.
author: dependabot[bot]

title: Reject signatures with future `created` timestamps in Rust verifier
description: Adds fail-closed behavior for signatures whose `created` parameter is set in the future, matching the TypeScript `web-bot-auth` verifier behavior. Introduces a new `WebBotAuthError::SignatureCreatedInFuture` error variant and `is_created_in_future` field on `SecurityAdvisory`, returning the error before cryptographic verification when `created` is missing, unparsable, or in the future.
impact: Rust library consumers implementing `WebBotAuthVerifier::verify` must handle the new `WebBotAuthError::SignatureCreatedInFuture` error variant; previously valid signatures with future `created` timestamps will now be rejected.
author: SashaMIT
reasons: breaking, on shipped surface: signature-verification, defect-vocabulary

title: Fix tool execute steps missing targetDocument parameter
description: Corrects the tool definition's execute steps algorithm signature to include the missing `Document` `targetDocument` parameter alongside `inputArguments` and `completionSteps`. Updates all call sites—the tool execute steps algorithm and the imperative `registerTool` steps—to pass `targetDocument` consistently.
impact: Implementors of the tool execution pipeline must update their execute steps algorithms to accept and forward the `targetDocument` parameter as specified.
author: domfarolino

title: Improve JSON Schema Generation Pipeline with Bundling
description: Switches protoc JSON Schema generation from `target=json` to `target=json-bundle` output format and adds a Python post-processing script to clean up definition names by stripping package namespaces and `.jsonschema.json` suffixes. The pipeline now uses `$defs` (Draft 2020-12 compatible) instead of `definitions`, and updates all internal `$ref` references accordingly.
impact: Developers consuming the generated JSON Schema bundle will see cleaner definition names and `$defs` instead of `definitions`, but this only affects tooling/build scripts, not the protocol specification itself.
author: kthota-g

title: Define Location Context Behavior for Fulfillment Extension
description: Adds a new 'Location Context' section to the Fulfillment specification that defines how `context.location` interacts with `filters.fulfills_to` and `selected_destination_id` across Catalog and Checkout. The section clarifies precedence rules, field roles, and how a location identifier carries forward from Catalog discovery through Cart to Checkout. Schema descriptions are updated to align with the new terminology and cross-references.
impact: Developers implementing Fulfillment-extended Catalog or Checkout capabilities must align their `context.location` handling with the defined precedence rules, ensuring `filters.fulfills_to` supersedes `context` for destination/availability resolution and `selected_destination_id` governs over `context.location` once set.
author: igrigorik
reasons: payment on defect-vocabulary, ap2-mandate-instrument, commerce-observation, discovery

title: Change executeTool() input from JSON string to object
description: The `executeTool()` method signature was updated to accept a plain JavaScript object (`object inputObject`) instead of a `DOMString` JSON string. The serialization to JSON string now happens internally within the method steps, using the standard 'serializing a JavaScript value to a JSON string' algorithm.
impact: Developers calling `executeTool()` must update their code to pass a plain object (e.g., `{a: 10}`) instead of a JSON-encoded string (e.g., `"{a: 10}"`), as the old string-based signature is no longer accepted.
author: beaufortfrancois

title: Fix normative defects in tool registration and observation
description: Corrects four normative bugs in the specification: fixes descendant navigable traversal to use inclusive variants, corrects tool map access syntax for internal context, fixes an inverted assertion for document active state, and removes an erroneous possessive apostrophe in a let statement. These are specification correctness fixes with no semantic intent changes.
impact: Implementers following the specification will now get correct behavior for tool registration, document notifications, and observation algorithms that previously contained contradictory or malformed normative steps.
author: emecii

title: Fix Broken Links in Documentation Index
description: Replaces raw HTML anchor tags with MkDocs markdown button syntax for the hero section's 'Get started' and 'Read the spec' links. The fix also restructures the hero section HTML to properly close and reopen the div container, resolving broken link rendering in the documentation site.
impact: Documentation readers will now see correctly rendered and functional navigation buttons on the index page.
author: keraron

title: Add Payment Terms and Schedules to Checkout Specification
description: Introduces a new `dev.ucp.shopping.payment_terms` capability that adds `terms[]` and `selected_term_id` to `checkout.payment`, enabling businesses to offer structured payment schedules (e.g., deposits, installments, Net-30). Includes new JSON schemas for `payment_term` and `payment_schedule` types, a `payment_term_changed` warning code, and comprehensive specification documentation covering selection flow, disclosure requirements, and instrument eligibility rules.
impact: Developers implementing checkout integrations can optionally adopt payment terms support; existing checkouts without terms are unaffected, but platforms wishing to present payment timing options must handle the new `terms[]` array and `selected_term_id` field.
author: raginpirate

title: Change RegisteredTool inputSchema from string to object
description: The `RegisteredTool#inputSchema` field type is changed from `DOMString` to `object`, returning a parsed JavaScript object instead of a raw JSON string. The spec now requires parsing the stored JSON string using the standard JSON-to-JS-value algorithm when exposing the tool, and notes this parse will never throw since the stored value is always valid JSON.
impact: Developers consuming `RegisteredTool#inputSchema` must update their code, as the field now returns a parsed JavaScript object instead of a JSON string, requiring removal of any manual `JSON.parse()` calls.
author: beaufortfrancois

title: Add executeTool() API specification and documentation
description: Formally specifies the `executeTool()` and `getTools()` APIs in the WebMCP spec, including the `pending tool execution` struct, unloading document cleanup steps, imperative and declarative execute step algorithms, and AbortSignal-based cancellation support. The spec also defines how pending executions are cleaned up when caller or target documents are unloaded, and how tool unregistration cancels in-flight executions.
impact: Developers implementing in-page agents or tool execution flows should reference the newly specified `executeTool()` API, including AbortSignal cancellation and `toolchange` event handling patterns.
author: domfarolino

title: Fix AbortSignal Registration Order After exposedTo Validation
description: Reorders the `registerTool` algorithm to validate `exposedTo` origins before creating the promise and registering the `AbortSignal` algorithm. This prevents abort steps from being added when the method would subsequently throw due to invalid `exposedTo` values, ensuring the signal handler is only registered after all validation passes.
impact: Implementors of the `registerTool` API will observe corrected behavior where `AbortSignal` handlers are not registered if `exposedTo` validation fails, eliminating a potential resource leak or inconsistent state.
author: beaufortfrancois

title: Fix Typo and Clarify Metadata Description in Spec
description: Corrects minor wording issues in the metadata section of the specification document. The phrase 'any valid value that can be represented in JSON' is simplified to 'any valid JSON value', and the link formatting for Extensions is corrected from bracket-escaped to standard markdown.
impact: No impact on implementors; purely a documentation clarification with no behavioral or structural changes.
author: torin96

title: Add Rotating Tagline Carousel to Documentation Homepage
description: Replaces the static hero tagline on the docs index page with an animated carousel cycling through three distinct taglines every 6 seconds. Includes accessible dot navigation controls, CSS fade transitions, and respects the `prefers-reduced-motion` media query.
impact: Documentation site visitors will see a rotating tagline on the homepage; no impact on protocol implementers or API consumers.
author: keraron

title: Add Glossary and Split Payments to llms.txt Index
description: Adds two previously missing entries to the llms.txt plugin configuration in mkdocs.yml: the Glossary page (with descriptions of key protocol terms) and the Split Payments Extension page (covering multi-instrument checkout semantics). This ensures these specification pages are included in the LLM-readable site index.
impact: Documentation consumers and LLM-based tooling will now have indexed access to the Glossary and Split Payments specification pages, with no impact on protocol implementers.
author: yingzhehu-TT

title: Add Lodging TC Formation Announcement to Documentation
description: Adds an announcement entry for the formation of the Lodging Technical Council (Lodging TC) dated August 11, 2026, listing inaugural members including Amadeus, Booking.com, Expedia, Google, Hilton, Marriott, and Trip.com. Also updates the spell-check custom words list with the new company names referenced in the announcement.
impact: Documentation readers and stakeholders following UCP governance will see the new Lodging TC formation announcement on the announcements page.
author: carolinerg1

title: Add location context hint to platform-initiated requests
description: Adds an optional `location` field to the context schema in shopping types, allowing platforms to pass a stable, opaque identifier for a physical location (e.g., store, restaurant, pickup point) as a non-binding hint. A corresponding glossary entry for 'Location' is also added to document the concept formally.
impact: Developers implementing platform-initiated shopping requests can now optionally include a location identifier in the context object to enable location-aware personalization and recommendations.
author: jingyli

title: Rust verifier now fails closed on expired signatures
description: The `WebBotAuthVerifier::verify` method now rejects signatures with expired or unparsable `expires` parameters before performing cryptographic verification, matching the behavior of the TypeScript `http-message-sig` verifier. A new opt-in method `verify_ignore_expiry` is added for callers that need to perform cryptographic verification on expired signatures and handle expiry themselves via a returned `SecurityAdvisory`.
impact: Rust callers using `WebBotAuthVerifier::verify` that previously succeeded on expired test vectors will now receive `WebBotAuthError::SignatureIsExpired`; they must either ensure signatures are valid within their expiry window or migrate to the new `verify_ignore_expiry` method.
author: SashaMIT
reasons: breaking, on shipped surface: signature-verification, defect-vocabulary

title: Add Task Generation Field for Ordering, Polling, and Concurrency
description: Introduces a `generation` field to the `Task` message, incrementing by exactly 1 on every state-changing mutation. This enables clients to detect missed events via sequence gaps, perform efficient long-polling via `currentGeneration` on `GetTaskRequest`, and implement optimistic concurrency control via `ifGenerationMatch` on `SendMessageConfiguration`. A new `TaskGenerationMismatchError` (HTTP 409 / gRPC ABORTED) is defined for concurrency violations.
impact: Developers implementing A2A clients or servers can optionally adopt generation-based event ordering, long-polling, and optimistic concurrency; existing implementations continue to interoperate since `generation` defaults to 0 in proto3 and all new fields are optional.
author: Tehsmash

title: Fix Broken Intra-Document Anchor Links in Docs
description: Corrects multiple broken anchor links across the specification and topic documentation files. The fixes update outdated or incorrect section fragment identifiers to match current heading anchors in the specification document.
impact: Developers reading the protocol documentation will now have working navigation links to the correct specification sections.
author: msrivastav13

title: Define Deterministic Operating Hours for Location Service
description: This PR formalizes the semantics of `hours` and `exception_hours` fields in the Location service, introducing explicit rules for schedule evaluation including DST handling, split shifts, exception precedence, and closure representation. It adds a dedicated 'Operating Hours' section to the spec with evaluation algorithms, Business/Platform compliance guidelines, and concrete examples. Schema types for `daily_hour`, `exception_hour`, `time_interval`, and `location_filter` are updated to align with the new deterministic rules.
impact: Businesses emitting location schedules must conform to the new deterministic rules (e.g., valid `opens`/`closes` pairs, non-intersecting exception ranges, required `timezone`), and Platforms evaluating schedules must use the Location's `timezone` and apply the specified DST and split-shift semantics.
author: igrigorik

title: Simplify payment schedule amounts and terms structure
description: Replaces the `schedules[].totals` array (which required a `type: total` entry) with a single scalar `schedules[].amount` field, simplifying the payment schedule schema. Also clarifies rules around when `terms` and `selected_term_id` must be present, restricts multi-schedule terms to a single funding instrument, and requires term-driven price differences (discounts/fees) to appear explicitly in `checkout.totals`.
impact: Businesses and Platforms implementing payment terms must update their integrations to use `schedules[].amount` instead of `schedules[].totals`, and must surface term-related price adjustments in `checkout.totals` rather than implicitly through schedule sums.
author: raginpirate

title: Define Sale-Basis Steps and Quantity Units for Line Items
description: Introduces a formal sale-basis contract for quantities across cart, catalog, checkout, and order flows, defining how `quantity_unit` descriptors (unit, scale, increment) denominate integer step counts. Specifies rules for basis discovery, assertion matching, mismatch handling (visible conversion or recoverable rejection), and response echoing. Adds `quantity_unit` to variant, item, line item, and order line item schemas.
impact: Developers implementing cart, checkout, catalog, or order integrations must handle `quantity_unit` descriptors on line items and variants, update quantity interpretation logic to use scale-based step counts, and implement mismatch recovery flows for sale-basis assertion failures.
author: igrigorik

title: Add --frozen flag to uv run pre-commit hooks
description: Adds the `--frozen` flag to all three `uv run` commands in the pre-commit configuration, preventing uv from updating the lockfile during hook execution. This ensures pre-commit hooks run with pinned dependencies rather than potentially modifying the environment.
impact: Developers using these pre-commit hooks will now run validation scripts with frozen dependencies, ensuring consistent and reproducible hook behavior without unintended lockfile modifications.
author: damaz91

title: Reserve `ucp` Protocol Namespace and Add `map_order` for Registry Ordering
description: Reserves the `ucp` member name as the protocol namespace across all structured UCP object scopes, formally defining its semantics, openness rules, and ambient vocabulary. Introduces the `map_order` annotation within the `ucp` namespace to specify preferred ordering for registry map entries, and updates schema authoring guidelines, glossary, and AP2 mandate coverage accordingly.
impact: Schema authors and implementers must not declare domain fields named `ucp` in structured objects, and must reference `ucp.json#/$defs/members` when closing nested structured objects; consumers should update to ignore unrecognized `ucp` members and optionally honor `map_order` for registry display ordering.
author: igrigorik
reasons: mandate on defect-vocabulary, ap2-mandate-instrument, commerce-observation, discovery

title: Add Browser Implementation Status Tracking Document
description: Adds a new `implementation-status.md` file documenting WebMCP's current browser support across Brave, Chrome, Edge, Firefox, and Safari. Includes links to origin trials, standards positions, and browser-specific tracking issues. Updates README to reference the new document.
impact: Developers evaluating WebMCP adoption can now quickly assess browser support status and find relevant origin trial and standards tracking links.
author: beaufortfrancois

title: Add ADR-002 for Coherent Task History Design
description: Introduces ADR-002 documenting the architectural decision to add an ordered `timeline` collection plus generation-range-annotated `artifacts` to provide coherent, replayable task history in A2A v1.1. The ADR soft-deprecates `TaskStatus.message` in favor of role-tagged timeline entries and defers a fully unified event-sourced model to v2. An optional `elicitations` collection is proposed for input-required flows without altering existing task states.
impact: Protocol implementers and SDK authors should review the proposed v1.1 schema additions (timeline, artifact generation ranges, elicitations) to plan implementation, as these additive changes will affect how task history is constructed and consumed.
author: herczyn

title: Fix Missing contextId Field in Streaming Examples
description: Adds the missing `contextId` field to three streaming response event examples in the specification documentation (`task`, `artifactUpdate`, and `statusUpdate` events). This corrects the documentation to accurately reflect the actual protocol format where `contextId` is a required field in streaming event payloads.
impact: Developers referencing the streaming examples for implementation will now see accurate event structures that include the `contextId` field, reducing potential confusion or incorrect implementations.
author: juanferrub

title: Fix Grammar Error in Metadata Section
description: Removes a duplicate word ('and') in the Metadata section of the specification, correcting 'Metadata keys and are strings' to 'Metadata keys are strings'. This is a purely editorial fix with no technical changes.
impact: No functional impact; readers of the specification will encounter grammatically correct documentation.
author: dongjiang1989

title: Add Noorle to A2A Community Integrations List
description: Adds Noorle as a community integration in the A2A documentation and updates the Pydantic AI documentation link. Also updates the spell-checker allowlist to include the Noorle brand name.
impact: Developers browsing the A2A community integrations page will now see Noorle as an available framework option with a direct link to its A2A documentation.
author: scollins99

title: Switch Pre-commit Hooks to Use uv for Python
description: Updates `.pre-commit-config.yaml` to invoke Python scripts via `uv run python` instead of `python3`, ensuring local pre-commit hooks use the project's Python version defined in `pyproject.toml` rather than the system Python. This affects all three validation hooks: changed-file validation, full-corpus validation, and validator unit tests.
impact: Contributors running pre-commit hooks locally will now require `uv` installed; hooks will consistently use the project-defined Python version instead of the system Python.
author: horaceewang-TT

title: Add Per-Language SDK Repository Links to Site Header
description: Adds a row of per-language SDK repository links (Python, Go, Java, JS, .NET, Rust) to the MkDocs site header by overriding the Material theme's header partial. The existing single repo_url/repo_name config is disabled in favor of this custom SDK links row, which mirrors the layout used on adk.dev.
impact: Documentation site visitors will see quick-access SDK repository links in the header; no changes to the protocol specification itself, so implementers are unaffected.
author: msampathkumar

title: Add Payment Terms with Simple Schedules Support
description: Introduces a redesigned Payment Terms extension replacing `available_terms[]`/`instruments[].term_refs[]` with `terms[]` and `selected_term_id` on `checkout.payment`. The new design simplifies term selection to a single buyer choice (similar to fulfillment options), removes instrument-to-schedule assignment, and restricts schedule types to a single well-known value (`immediate`) while deprecating recurrence rules in favor of explicit per-schedule entries. Documentation is substantially rewritten to clarify presentation requirements, disclosure obligations, and term selection lifecycle.
impact: Platform developers implementing payment flows must update their integration to use `terms[]` and `selected_term_id` instead of the previous `available_terms[]` and `term_refs[]` fields, and handle the new `payment_term_changed` warning code in `messages[]`.

title: Add Payment Term Selection to Checkout Flow

Introduces term selection as a checkout mutation with authoritative server-side recomputation, adds disclosure obligations via existing policy/warning mechanisms, and simplifies instrument constraints by removing per-schedule funding references.
impact: Developers implementing payment terms must migrate from `available_terms[]` and `term_refs[]` to the new `terms[]` and `selected_term_id` fields, update checkout mutation flows to handle term selection and `payment_term_changed` warnings, and remove any discovery-time handler profiles that reference term IDs.

Third-party extensions and payment handlers are explicitly distinguished as independently versioned.
impact: Implementers and schema authors benefit from clearer versioning rules distinguishing UCP lockstep-versioned components from independently versioned third-party extensions and payment handlers, requiring no changes to existing implementations.

impact: Developers using the example validation scripts will see more accurate error suppression behavior when array examples contain `"..."` ellipsis sentinels mixed with real objects.

impact: Developers implementing in-task authorization flows should review their handling of `TASK_STATE_AUTH_REQUIRED` to ensure they are not incorrectly treating the state transition as an implicit authorization grant for subsequent operations.

New authoring guidelines document how extension authors should define Action types, config schemas, fallback behavior, and retry semantics.

impact: Platform implementors must update their namespace validation logic to use the new derivation algorithm (reversing the `schema` URL host and checking label-prefix alignment), stop validating `spec` URL origins, and reject any entity whose `schema` URL fails the binding before fetching it.
